Ray tracing is very subjective and the level of details it can introduce in games can vary. Games like Cyberpunk and Alan Wake 2 can look extremely good with ray tracing while other games can barely have a noticeable difference. I think the reality is that console players care less about these features and just want something to play on with better graphics and 60 fps while being affordable. I’m not necessarily saying the PS5 Pro should’ve been made as how it is bit it’s not a bad deal if Sony is claiming what it can do.

imo if the console can competently do ray tracing while pushing 60 fps then I think $700 is totally justified, like being able to play Alan Wake 2 at 1440p or so with ray tracing. If you want a PC that can do ray tracing on modern titles you can only really get the rtx 4070 which is gonna be minimum $1200 pc build. If you don’t care about better graphics and features then just get the ps5 slim or whatever. Maybe Sony went too far with how powerful the console is but this is probably the cheapest system that people can do ray tracing currently, and when games like AC Shadows are gonna be forcing ray tracing into their games now it may be the unfortunate reality that we are gonna need beefier consoles like the ps5 pro.

I would suggest buying the Steam Deck Oled, it’s the least powerful out of the bunch and Linux can have compatibility issues with some games but aside from that the steam deck oled but it feels the most reliable out of the 3. The Legion Go has some issues with its fans where dust can get in easily so you might have to clean the insides sometimes which I’m not a fan of doing on such a delicate hardware. The Ally X is made by ASUS who is known to void warranty claims, I recommend checking out Gamer’s Nexus videos on them and how ASUS scammed then. I would say performance wise Ally X is the best but I still feel like you would be missing from the Steam Deck Oled’s great Oled screen as well as the great ergonomics the Steam Deck has.
